main_text.p: ben Esdræ. Sed dissertissimè interpretatio mea fert, libros illos omnes fuisse ἐκτύπως[?] & copias unius illius libri à Mordochæo scripti.

4. Ex pag. 80 בבואה male versi introitum, significat enim imaginem, vel potius ibi personam hominis, qui se ipsum in speculo videt, ita loqui solemus, unde Virgilius, non sum adeo informis, nuper me in littore vidi Ideo statim colligit אתה משנה עצמך mutas te ipsum personam tuam, &c. Clara hæc sunt ex lectione textus. Significatio umbræ, quam illi das, textui convenire non potest. Legi Rabbinum quemdam Nephtali Herts dictum, qui voces difficiles Midras Raboth & Megiloth explicavit, interpretatur similiter צל sed argumento textus magis favet introitus tuus quàm umbra tua. Eodem sensu legitur בובא in eodem Midras Raboth super numer' Parascha 10. versus finem כאיתי אתה בובא שלי בתוך חמים [illegible, ~2 letters] לפחן יצרי
5. Expag. 265. Librum iterum con-suli, omnia se habent, ut ea excerpsi,

page.notes: The Hebrew and Greek were copied from the scan with some doubt: the Greek word after "fuisse" (marked [?]), the Hebrew "בובא" in the fourth and fifth lines, and the Hebrew line before "לפחן יצרי", where one group of letters is unreadable and marked [illegible, ~2 letters]. The "numer'" mark is copied as printed. The Hebrew in the first and second lines and the word "צל" are clear.
